attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry is the same soldier: of Tyana, in the years of the persecutions under Diocletian, a guard over the prisons who was himself a Christian without his officers or fellow soldiers knowing it, and who used his position to bring food to the martyrs; six venerable ascetics were brought in — there had been a seventh, who died on the road of old age and hardship — and when the judge asked where their seventh companion was, Varus cried «ἰδοὺ ἐγώ», here am I. He died under very savage torture without changing his faith, the ascetics were beheaded the next day, and Christian hands buried the seven at night. **No `dates` proposed**: the only year on the page hangs on a reign — «στα χρόνια των διωγμών επί Διοκλητιανού» — and the page gives no figure of its own; the reign is in the life paragraph instead. The page records a fragment of his relics at the monastery of Kykkos in Cyprus. The Ἀπολυτίκιον is taken and it names him. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.11.2026 (19. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Вар.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, one person, quoted whole with its closing full stop (section 4). «муч.» is the `martyr` this folder holds and the body’s «римски официр» the `soldier`, so `types` is untouched. NO `dates`, AND THE ENTRY GIVES NO YEAR AT ALL. This folder held none and holds none; there is nothing in the entry to date it by — no emperor, no consul, no number. Said here because an absence is worth recording once. THE PROLOGUE SAYS SEVEN WHERE THIS CORPUS HAS SIX, AND THAT IS THE READING OF THE DAY. Varus is already related to `six-hermit-martyrs`. This entry has SEVEN Christian teachers thrown into prison, whom Varus visited, supplied and served eagerly, wishing he could be a martyr himself and ashamed that fear prevented him. ONE OF THE SEVEN DIED IN THE PRISON. So when the prince had the martyrs brought out he counted SIX and asked where the seventh was — and Varus answered «Ја сам седми!», I am the seventh. That is how a company of six and a seventh man who is not one of them come to be one feast, and it explains the corpus’s own count rather than contradicting it. No new `related` row is owed: the row is already there, both ways. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. He was A ROMAN OFFICER IN EGYPT AND A SECRET CHRISTIAN. The manner of his death is given in full: stripped and beaten with DRY STAVES, then tied to a tree while they CUT THE FLESH OFF HIM PIECE BY PIECE WITH KNIVES until he gave up his soul, and HIS BODY THROWN ON A DUNGHILL. And then the whole of the Cleopatra story, which is why this folder relates her and her son already: a woman of Palestine, the WIDOW OF AN OFFICER, who took the relics off the dunghill in secret and buried them IN HER OWN LODGING; who then asked the prince’s leave to carry her dead husband’s body home from Egypt to Palestine and WAS GRANTED IT AT ONCE BECAUSE SHE WAS AN OFFICER’S WIFE; AND WHO CARRIED THE MARTYR’S RELICS INSTEAD OF HER HUSBAND’S. She brought them to her native village of ЕДРА NEAR TABOR, buried them honourably, and afterwards RAISED A CHURCH TO HIM; and Varus appeared to her often from the other world, bright as an angel of God. No `office`, no `locations`: Egypt, Palestine, Tabor and a village are named and none is a coordinate. THE FORM IS FREE: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Вар», which is three letters and therefore BELOW `nameKeys`’s four-letter minimum — it will not enter the fold index at all, which is a different thing from folding onto nothing and is worth saying once. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Uar, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

english.text: Thy martyr Varus, O Lord, in his contest received from Thee our God the crown of incorruption; for having Thy strength he brought the torturers low, and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At his prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Τῶν Μαρτύρων ζηλώσας τὰ κατορθώματα, μαρτυρικῶς ἠγωνίσω ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης Χριστοῦ, καὶ καθεῖλες τὸν ἐχθρὸν παμμάκαρ Οὔαρε, ἐν γὰρ ἰκρίω προσδεθεῖς, πρὸς τῷ ξύλῳ τῆς ζωῆς, νομίμως ἀποκατέστης, πρεσβευτικὴ χορηγία, καταφαιδρύνων τᾶς ψυχᾶς ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’. Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the only hymn on the page of «Άγιος Ούαρος», and it names him.

english.text: Emulating the achievements of the Martyrs, you contended as a martyr for the glory of Christ and pulled the enemy down, all-blessed Varus; for bound upon the frame you were lawfully restored to the tree of life, and by the bounty of your intercession you make our souls bright.

hymns.text: Воинством святых страстотерпец страждущих законне,/ зря онех, показал еси мужески крепость свою./ И устремився на страсть волею,/ и умрети вожделе за Христа,/ Иже приял еси почесть победы твоего страдания, Уаре,/ моли спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 октября ст. ст. — «Тропарь мученика Уара»

english.text: Beholding the host of holy passion-bearers contending lawfully, you showed your own strength manfully; and setting out willingly upon suffering you longed to die for Christ, from whom you received the honour of victory for your suffering, O Varus. Pray that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Христу последуя, мучениче Уаре,/ Того испив чашу,/ и мучения венцем увязеся,/ и со Ангелы ликовствуеши:// моли непрестанно за души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 октября ст. ст. — «Кондак мученика Уара»

english.text: Following Christ, O martyr Varus, you drank his cup, were wreathed with the crown of martyrdom, and now keep festival with the angels: pray unceasingly for our souls.
